main_text.p: Non unquā subeant castum scelera improba pectus Iniusti, nec mens, facta nefanda probet.
Gaudet quippe Deus syncero pectore: & inde Tristia (non falsò) fata superbus habet.
Fas numerare pijs longæua ætate nepotes: At primo sentit, funera, flore, malus.
Iusto iusta Deo sunt curæ: & cultor honesti Præmia in innumera posteritate capit.
Est præsens Numen sanctis, & robore firmat, Incutiant ne quem, sæua pericla, metum.
Nam vt lingua sacrâm sonat imperterrita legem: Sic unum mentes Numen honore colunt.
Hinc non insidias horrent scelerumq; tribunal, Nec fera peruersi iudicis ora timent.
Quippe Dei secum referunt in corde fauorem, Quo, facilè expirat, corda calente, timor.
Tu ne cede malis, sed contrà audentior ito: Non procul est, durum qui releuabit onus.
Te tua tunc, Superis charum, super æthera virtus Tollet, & innocuo corde patebit honos.
Fide Deo, & dabitur manifesta in luce uidere, Post paulò, pessum, funditùs, ire, malum.
Vidi ego surgentis, florentem, palmitis instar Iniustum, exiguo tempore nullus erat.
Non uana est Domini tantis cum uiribus ira: In nihilum, Iouæ quem premit ira, ruit.

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout. Some words in the scan are faint; "sacrâm" (line 6 of the fourth stanza group) and "Quo, facilè" are read with moderate confidence. Verse lines are printed in long lines and are transcribed as separate paragraphs by stanza where the printer's line breaks marked the stanza divisions; the original reads as continuous verse, so paragraph breaks here follow the printed couplets.
